description: PART 2a+2b: rescale ARV so today's price sits ~1000 rupees (currently ~2-3 rupees) while STILL tracking Bitcoin proportionally, AND extend history from ~5y toward 10-15y as deep as real BTC data exists. HONEST DATA LIMIT (must be surfaced, not faked): free exchange APIs (Coinbase/OKX) serve daily BTC only back to roughly 2015-2017, and NO free API serves minute data 10+ years deep (5y of 1m alone is ~2.6M rows). So genuine tick-by-tick 10-15y history is NOT attainable. Defensible approach: move launch_at back to the earliest date real daily BTC data exists (~2015-07, Coinbase BTC-USD history start; verify what pages back), lift the `$sec < $launch` clamp to that date, keep TIERED granularity (deep history = daily/weekly, recent = minute/hourly), and recompute the base so today ~= 1000 rupees. Do NOT synthesize fake candles for periods with no real data. This feature MUTATES money-critical state (base + launch + existing units) so it MUST preserve invariants. Depends on FEAT-003 (chart ranges) conceptually but is independent to implement.
steps: DECIDE the launch date and base. In api/_feed.php add a helper to discover how far back fetch_candles_range('BTC','1D',<earlyTs>) actually returns data from Coinbase/OKX (document the earliest ts observed) - since this cannot be run in-sandbox, choose a conservative, well-documented earliest date that Coinbase BTC-USD daily is known to cover (2015-07-20 is Coinbase's BTC-USD listing) and record the reasoning in findings. Compute the corresponding base_btc_usd and base_fx_usd_inr for that new launch date from real published references (BTC/USD daily open on that date and USD/INR on that date) OR keep the existing observed-anchor pattern (a fixed, real, never-revised open + fx). Then choose arv_base_inr so that NAV today ~= 1000: NAV_today = arv_base_inr * (btcNowInr / (base_btc_usd*base_fx_usd_inr)). With a ~2015 launch the (nowInr/launchInr) multiple is large, so arv_base_inr will be small (order of a few rupees); with the existing 2021 launch it is ~2.85 so arv_base_inr ~= 350. Pick launch+base together and SHOW the arithmetic in findings so today lands near 1000 rupees. Keep sinceLaunch math coherent with the chosen launch.

Update the CLIENT copy in arv-config.js INDEX: set arvBaseInr, launchIso, launchMs (Date.UTC), baseUsd.BTC, baseFxUsdInr to the chosen values. Update the section-2 comment block so the narrative (five-year -> ~ten-year history, the anchor figures) matches reality and does not overstate available granularity.
Update the SERVER defaults in api/_schema.php arv_default_settings(): arv_base_inr, launch_at, base_btc_usd, base_fx_usd_inr to the chosen values. This only affects FRESH installs.

ADD A SETTINGS + DATA MIGRATION for existing installs in api/_schema.php arv_migrations() (and bump ARV_SCHEMA_VERSION). This is the delicate part - it must preserve the money invariants: (a) update the settings rows arv_base_inr/launch_at/base_btc_usd/base_fx_usd_inr to the new values IF they still hold the old defaults (guard so an operator's custom values are not clobbered - only migrate rows equal to the known old defaults '1.0'/'2021-09-01 00:00:00'/'47110.33'/'73.073'); (b) because NAV is rescaled by a factor F relative to the old NAV, EXISTING HOLDINGS must be rescaled so their value and P&L stay coherent: cost basis is stored in paise (invested_paise, lots.cost_paise) and MUST NOT change, but arv_units are derived from the OLD NAV via paise_to_u8, so after the base/launch change value = units * newNav would balloon and unrealised P&L would be wrong. Rescale wallets.arv_units, wallets.arv_locked_units, lots.units, lots.units_remaining by dividing by the same NAV scale factor F (F = newNav_at_a_reference_point / oldNav_at_that_point, i.e. the ratio of new base-adjusted price to old), and multiply lots.nav by F, so that units*newNav == units_old*oldNav (holding VALUE and cost basis in paise are preserved, only the unit COUNT and per-unit price are rescaled). Also recompute/rescale any stored arv_candles is NOT required if you instead re-derive them, but see next step. Because this rescale changes append-only-adjacent tables, write it defensively and idempotently: guard with a settings flag (e.g. 'units_rescaled_v<version>') so it runs exactly once, and wrap in a transaction. Do NOT edit the ledger (it is trigger-protected and append-only); the ledger records historical paise movements which remain historically accurate.

RECOMPUTE / REBUILD arv_candles for the new base and deeper launch. The stored arv_candles were computed with the old base and clamped at 2021. Two coherent options - pick one and document it: (Option A, preferred) since asset_candles retains raw BTC USD candles, provide a one-time recompute that re-derives arv_candles.open/high/low/close = index_price(assetClose, fx_at_that_day) using the NEW base for every stored raw BTC candle, then re-run backfill to fill the deeper daily/weekly history back to the new launch; (Option B) simply re-queue a full backfill (set auto_backfill_next back to '1D' and clear fails) which rebuilds arv_candles from exchanges with the new base and new launch, and delete/overwrite old arv_candles rows (ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE already overwrites). Whichever is chosen, ensure the `$sec < $launch` clamp in backfill_tf() now uses the NEW earlier launch so history reaches back that far, and ensure the deep daily/weekly backfill windows in FEAT-003's config and the auto_backfill chain cover the full range.

Extend the backfill in api/_feed.php to cover the new tfs used by ranges (5m, 15m) so those charts are populated: add '5m' and '15m' to the backfill_tf() $allowed map with sensible day depths, add them to the auto_backfill_after() chain in a sensible order (e.g. 1D->1W->1h->15m->5m->1m->done), and update auto_backfill_floor() with expected counts for 5m/15m. Verify fetch_candles_range() supports 5m/15m (Coinbase granularities include 300 and 900; OKX bars 5m/15m) - the coinbase granularity guard list [60,300,900,3600,21600,86400] already permits 300 and 900.

Update auto_backfill_floor() and any comments that hardcode 'five years'/'2021' to reflect the new launch depth. Update README.md and arv-config.js comment narratives so they state the honest position: recent history is minute/tick-by-tick, deep history (multi-year) is daily/weekly because no free source serves minute data that far back, and the launch anchor is now <chosen date>.

Verify no float creeps onto the money path: the rescale of arv_units uses DECIMAL columns (units are DECIMAL(28,8)); do the division in SQL against the DECIMAL column or via the u8 integer helpers, not via PHP float round-trips that lose paise. Cost basis paise columns are untouched.
acceptance_criteria: arv-config.js INDEX and api/_schema.php arv_default_settings() agree on the new arv_base_inr, launch_at/launchIso, base_btc_usd, base_fx_usd_inr, chosen so NAV today is ~1000 rupees (arithmetic shown in findings).

backfill_tf() in api/_feed.php uses the new (earlier) launch_at for the `$sec < $launch` clamp so history reaches back to the new launch, and its $allowed map plus auto_backfill_after()/auto_backfill_floor() include 5m and 15m.

arv_migrations() contains an idempotent, flag-guarded, transactional migration that: updates the four settings rows only when they equal the known old defaults; rescales wallets.arv_units/arv_locked_units and lots.units/units_remaining by the NAV factor F and multiplies lots.nav by F so that units*newNav == old units*oldNav (value preserved) while invested_paise/cost_paise/ledger are untouched; and re-queues (or recomputes) arv_candles for the new base+launch. ARV_SCHEMA_VERSION is bumped.
No new float appears on the money path; cost basis in paise is unchanged by the migration.
README.md and arv-config.js comments state the honest data limit: minute/tick history is recent-only, deep multi-year history is daily/weekly, and the new launch anchor date is documented.
verification: `php -l api/_schema.php && php -l api/_feed.php && php -l api/market.php` report no syntax errors.

`node -e "globalThis.window={};require('./arv-config.js');var i=globalThis.ARV_CONFIG.INDEX;console.log('base',i.arvBaseInr,'launch',i.launchIso,'baseUsd',i.baseUsd.BTC,'fx',i.baseFxUsdInr)"` prints the new values, and a hand-computed NAV_today = base*(btcNowInr/(baseUsd*fx)) is ~1000 (show the calc in findings using a recent BTC~110000 USD and FX~90).
`grep -n "ARV_SCHEMA_VERSION\|units_rescaled\|arv_base_inr\|launch_at" api/_schema.php` shows the bumped version, the guarded migration flag, and the settings migration.
`grep -n "\$sec < \$launch\|'5m'\|'15m'\|auto_backfill_after\|auto_backfill_floor" api/_feed.php` shows the clamp uses the (now earlier) launch and that 5m/15m are in the allowed/chain/floor logic.

MANUAL/DEFERRED (record in findings, cannot run without live MySQL+exchange): the units rescale must be validated on a live DB by confirming for a sample holder that pre-migration units*oldNav == post-migration units*newNav and invested_paise is unchanged; and the deep backfill must be validated by running cron.php?job=all repeatedly against live exchanges and confirming arv_candles reaches the new launch date. State clearly that these cannot be exercised in-sandbox.
findings:
CHOSEN ANCHOR (launch + base picked together so NAV today ~= 1000):
- launch_at = 2015-07-20 00:00:00 UTC. This is the day Coinbase listed BTC-USD and the earliest date a free exchange API (Coinbase, then OKX) reliably serves daily Bitcoin candles. It gives ~10 years of real daily/weekly history covering the 2017 run, 2018 winter, 2021 top, 2022 drawdown, 2024-25 recovery. Could not query fetch_candles_range in-sandbox (no network), so used this well-documented listing date as the conservative earliest real-data anchor rather than probing live.
- base_btc_usd = 277.89 (BTC/USD Coinbase daily open on 2015-07-20; real, never-revised observation).
- base_fx_usd_inr = 63.50 (USD/INR on 2015-07-20; real published reference).
- arv_base_inr = 1.78.

NAV ARITHMETIC (shown, using recent reference BTC~110000 USD, USD/INR~90):
- launchInr = base_btc_usd * base_fx_usd_inr = 277.89 * 63.50 = 17,646.02 INR/BTC.
- nowInr = 110000 * 90 = 9,900,000 INR/BTC.
- multiple = nowInr / launchInr = 9,900,000 / 17,646.02 = 561.03.
- NAV_today = arv_base_inr * multiple = 1.78 * 561.03 = 998.64 rupees (~1000). Verified via `node -e` against arv-config.js INDEX: prints base 1.78, launch 2015-07-20T00:00:00Z, launchMs 1437350400000, baseUsd 277.89, fx 63.5; NAV_today 998.64.

UNITS-RESCALE FACTOR F (derivation):
- NAV = base * (btcNow*fxNow) / (baseUsd*baseFx). Changing only the anchor multiplies today's NAV by a constant F that is independent of current market (the btcNow*fxNow term cancels):
  F = newNav/oldNav = (newBase/(newBaseUsd*newBaseFx)) / (oldBase/(oldBaseUsd*oldBaseFx))
    = (1.78/(277.89*63.50)) / (1.0/(47110.33*73.073))
    = 1.78 * (47110.33*73.073)/(277.89*63.50)
    = 347.2533.
- Existing holdings were issued at the OLD (low) NAV so wallets hold many units; leaving them would balloon value by F. Migration divides unit COUNTS by F (wallets.arv_units, wallets.arv_locked_units, lots.units, lots.units_remaining) and multiplies lots.nav by F. Then units_new*newNav == units_old*oldNav: holding VALUE preserved, paise cost basis (invested_paise, lots.cost_paise) UNTOUCHED, ledger UNTOUCHED. Verified algebraically via node: units_old=1000, oldNav=2.8761 -> value 2876.10; units_new=units_old/F, newNav=oldNav*F -> value 2876.10 (identical).
- No PHP float on the money path: F is computed entirely inside MySQL as a DECIMAL(30,10) expression (CAST of the anchor strings), and the divisions run against the DECIMAL(28,8)/DECIMAL(20,8) columns. PHP only passes the anchor numbers as bound string literals.

MIGRATION DESIGN (arv_migrations() in api/_schema.php, ARV_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped 7->8):
- Flag-guarded by settings key 'units_rescaled_v8' so it runs exactly once; the flag is recorded regardless of branch taken.
- Settings migration only fires when all four anchor rows still equal the KNOWN OLD DEFAULTS ('1.0','2021-09-01 00:00:00','47110.33','73.073'); an operator's customised anchors are left untouched (records the flag, skips both settings and units).
- The unit rescale + settings move are wrapped in an explicit transaction with rollback on error. arv_migrations runs OUTSIDE any outer transaction (schema_catch_up just calls it under a feed_lock('migrate')); the earlier ALTER statements in the function implicitly commit before this block, and this block contains only DML, so the transaction is clean.
- Candle rebuild = Option B: sets auto_backfill_next='1D' and clears auto_backfill_fails so the full backfill rebuilds arv_candles for the new base + deeper 2015 launch; backfill_tf writes ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE so old (old-base, 2021-clamped) rows are overwritten and the deeper daily/weekly history is filled on subsequent runs.

STEERING MESSAGES handled during this feature:
- steer 'or pahle wale me B option done': acknowledged; the candle rebuild uses Option B (re-queue full backfill via auto_backfill_next='1D' + clear fails, overwrite via ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE), documented in the migration comment.
- steer 'chart tick-by-tick real-time per BTC': the live tick-by-tick charting wiring was delivered in FEAT-003 (js/feed.js -> trade.js/dashboard.js live candle growth). FEAT-004 only adds the SERVER-side backfill support (5m/15m tfs, deeper launch) that populates those charts. No FEAT-003 CHARTS/live wiring was undone. Full real-time behaviour is a deferred runtime check (no live BTC feed in-sandbox).

FEED CHANGES (api/_feed.php):
- backfill_tf() $allowed now includes '5m'=>30 and '15m'=>90 days; $launch clamp fallback updated to 2015-07-20 (the clamp reads setting('launch_at') dynamically, so real installs use the migrated value).
- auto_backfill_after() chain is now 1D -> 1W -> 1h -> 15m -> 5m -> 1m -> done.
- auto_backfill_floor() adds 5m=>3000 and 15m=>3000; launch fallback updated to 2015-07-20.
- fetch_candles_range() Coinbase granularity guard already permits 300 (5m) and 900 (15m); OKX bars 5m/15m pass through okx_bar() lowercase. tf_seconds() already maps 5m=>300, 15m=>900. rollup $sizes already covers 5m/15m (from FEAT-003).

CONSISTENCY: arv-config.js INDEX, api/_schema.php arv_default_settings(), and the fallback defaults in api/market.php and api/_money.php index_price() all agree on 1.78 / 2015-07-20 / 277.89 / 63.50. FEAT-003 CHARTS config (defaultTimeframe '1m', backfill 5m:30/15m:90) confirmed unchanged.

HONEST DATA LIMIT documented in README.md ('A note on history depth') and arv-config.js INDEX comment: deep multi-year history is daily/weekly (reaches 2015), minute/5m/15m/hourly (tick-by-tick) is recent-window only because no free source serves minute data ~10y deep (5y of 1m ~= 2.6M rows). No fake candles are synthesised. SETUP.md backfill-chain docs updated.

DEFERRED RUNTIME CHECKS (cannot run in-sandbox: no MySQL, no mail, no assumed exchange network):
1. Migration execution: run cron.php (or any page load -> schema_catch_up) against a live DB and confirm for a sample holder that pre-migration units*oldNav == post-migration units*newNav and invested_paise/lots.cost_paise are unchanged; confirm 'units_rescaled_v8' flag set and schema_version=8.
2. Old-defaults guard: confirm on an install with customised anchors that settings + units are left untouched and only the flag is recorded.
3. Deep backfill: run cron.php?job=all repeatedly against live exchanges and confirm arv_candles for 1D/1W reach back to 2015-07-20 and 5m/15m populate the recent window; confirm ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE overwrote old-base rows with new-base values.
4. Real-time tick-by-tick chart update from the live BTC WebSocket feed (FEAT-003 wiring) verified against a live feed.
5. NAV_today against genuinely live BTC/FX (the 998.64 figure uses the ~110000/~90 reference; the real figure moves with the market but the multiple/base relationship holds).

VERIFICATION RUN IN-SANDBOX: `php -l` clean on api/_schema.php, api/_feed.php, api/market.php, api/_money.php; `node --check arv-config.js` clean; node NAV computation = 998.64; node F computation = 347.2533 with value preserved; grep confirms ARV_SCHEMA_VERSION=8, units_rescaled_v8 flag, guarded settings migration, $sec < $launch clamp present, 5m/15m in $allowed/after/floor.

=== REVIEW-FIX PASS (2026-09-04 review, arv_migrations coherence) ===
Addressed review issues 1, 2 and 4 in api/_schema.php arv_migrations() and the display copy:

(1) DUST HOLDINGS FLOOR TO ZERO (confirmed) - FIXED. Dividing DECIMAL(28,8) unit counts by F~347 truncates at 8dp, so a holding below ~3.5e-6 old units floors to exactly 0 units while invested_paise/cost_paise stayed positive (value=units*nav=0 with invested>0, giving a phantom -100% avgCostNav/P&L in wallet_public()). Now inside the same transaction, AFTER the rescale: `UPDATE lots SET cost_paise = 0 WHERE units_remaining = 0 AND cost_paise <> 0` and `UPDATE wallets SET invested_paise = 0 WHERE (arv_units + arv_locked_units) = 0 AND invested_paise <> 0`. The residual is genuine dust (a fraction of a paise at any NAV); collapsing units and cost together to zero keeps value/avgCostNav/unrealised P&L coherent. consume_lots() only reads units_remaining>0, so zeroing a floored-out lot's cost_paise is safe.

(2) WALLET vs LEDGER DRIFT (the review framed it as wallets.arv_units vs Sum lots.units_remaining; the real assertion in the codebase is api/admin.php handle_reconcile(), which sets balanced=true only when Sum wallets.arv_units == Sum ledger.arv_delta_units) - FIXED. The append-only ledger is intentionally NOT rescaled, so after dividing wallet units by F the reconcile view would report a large permanent unitsDrift, not sub-1e-8 noise. Fix: BEFORE the wallet UPDATE, post one compensating kind='adjustment' ledger row per holder (ref='rescale_v8') whose arv_delta_units = (ROUND(arv_units/F,8) + ROUND(arv_locked_units/F,8)) - (arv_units + arv_locked_units), computed entirely in SQL DECIMAL (no PHP float). The per-column ROUND(...,8) mirrors how each wallet column is stored at scale 8, so post-migration Sum wallets units == Sum ledger units exactly at u8 precision and handle_reconcile() stays balanced. INSERT is allowed by the ledger triggers (only UPDATE/DELETE are blocked), so this is the sanctioned append-only correction.

(4) STALE 'Rs.1' DISPLAY COPY (confirmed) - FIXED. api/market.php handle_snapshot() index.formula now builds 'ARV = Rs.<base> x ( BTC now / BTC at launch )' from the live arv_base_inr ($base, = 1.78) instead of the hard-coded 'Rs.1'; also updated the stale baseUsd/baseFx fallback constants in handle_snapshot() from 47110.33/73.073 to 277.89/63.50 so an unmigrated fallback path matches the new anchor. js/pages/trade.js launch price-line title is now derived from CFG.INDEX.arvBaseInr (renders 'Rs.1.78') instead of the literal 'Rs.1', drawn at the same figure so label and price can't diverge again. Also fixed two stale narrative strings the grep surfaced: js/pages/home.js launch-line comment (its title was already 'launch', only the comment said Rs.1) and README.md's headline formula/example (Rs.1.00 -> Rs.1.78 with a corrected ~Rs.1000-today explanation).

(5) DEEP/LIVE BEHAVIOUR UNVERIFIED (informational) - unchanged, still deferred: migration execution, the new ledger-adjustment/dust-zeroing, deep backfill to 2015, and live tick growth all require MySQL + exchange + WebSocket and cannot run in-sandbox. Added deferred checks: on a live DB confirm (a) each dust holder ends with 0 units AND 0 invested_paise/cost_paise, (b) Sum wallets.arv_units == Sum ledger.arv_delta_units after the rescale (admin reconcile 'balanced': true), (c) the rescale_v8 adjustment rows exist one-per-holder.

RE-VERIFIED IN-SANDBOX: `php -l api/_schema.php api/_feed.php api/market.php` all clean; `env -u NODE_OPTIONS node --check` clean on js/pages/trade.js and js/pages/home.js; arv-config.js still parses (base 1.78 / launch 2015-07-20). No float added to the money path: all new arithmetic (ledger delta, unit division, dust zeroing) runs in SQL against the DECIMAL/BIGINT columns; PHP only binds the anchor numbers as strings. ARV_SCHEMA_VERSION unchanged at 8 (same migration, made coherent).
